docs.title: bixverse
docs.text:
A single cell suite for Python, with the numerics in the Rust crates underneath it: import bixverse as bv and you get QC, highly variable genes, PCA, neighbours, clustering, embeddings, differential expression, doublet detection, batch correction, metacells, annotation, ligand-receptor analysis, trajectories and multi-modal (WNN) workflows.

It's a port of the single cell suite of the bixverse R package.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
An experiment is a directory, and bv.SingleCells is a handle on it.

  • On-disk store. Two compressed binary files, cell-major and gene-major, memory-mapped on read. Counts never sit in memory as a whole. Methods pull the cells or genes they need from the right file.
  • DuckDB for obs and var. The cell and gene tables live in a DuckDB next to the store. sc.obs() and sc.var() hand you polars frames, sc.add_obs() writes columns back.
  • Cells to keep. QC doesn't delete anything. sc.set_cells_to_keep() decides which cells every downstream method sees, and you can reset it.
  • Rust numerics. Everything heavy runs in the extension. Python wraps it, validates the arguments and keeps the results (PCA, kNN, graph, embeddings) in a cache on the object that tracks what's stale.

The design choices are written up in the design vignette.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv pip install bixverse            # the suite: numpy, polars, duckdb
uv pip install "bixverse[embed]"   # UMAP, t-SNE, PHATE (manifolds-rs)
uv pip install "bixverse[plots]"   # bv.pl plots (matplotlib)
uv pip install "bixverse[gpu]"     # the bixverse-gpu wheel
uv pip install "bixverse[sparse]"  # scipy, for the scipy_csr exports
uv pip install "bixverse[torch]"   # torch, for bixverse.nn
uv pip install "bixverse[mlx]"     # MLX for bixverse.nn, Apple Silicon only
uv pip install "bixverse[jax]"     # JAX for bixverse.nn, CPU or CUDA

Extras combine: the quickstart needs "bixverse[embed,plots,sparse]".

docs.title: Thirty seconds
docs.text:
import bixverse as bv
import bixverse.embed

sc = bv.io.load_existing("my_experiment")

bv.pp.find_hvg(sc, hvg_no=2000)
bv.pp.calculate_pca(sc, no_pcs=30)
bv.graph.find_neighbours(sc)
bv.graph.find_clusters(sc, res=1.0, name="leiden_clusters")
bv.embed.umap(sc)

Building an experiment from MTX, h5ad, 10x h5 or an in-memory matrix is in the quickstart. The vignettes walk through the rest of the suite, the API reference has every function.

docs.title: Loader and scVI
docs.text:
The package started as a minibatch loader, and that part is still here. bv.CellReader opens the cell-major store and bv.CellLoader yields shuffled minibatches, sparse CSR by default. A feeder thread decodes ahead of your training step with the GIL released, so there is no Python-side decode and no materialised experiment.

bixverse.nn builds on it: a barebone scVI that trains straight off a store, on torch, MLX or JAX. See scVI.

docs.title: GPU wheel
docs.text:
bixverse-gpu (import bixverse_gpu) is a separate wheel with GPU twins of the CPU methods on wgpu. Modules mirror the CPU ones, take the same SingleCells and write the same cache slots (bar Harmony and fastMNN, which write harmony_gpu and mnn_gpu), so a pipeline swaps one import for the other:

import bixverse_gpu as bvg

bvg.pp.calculate_pca(sc, 30)
bvg.graph.find_neighbours(sc)

Without a GPU adapter the twins raise bixverse.BixverseError; bvg.gpu_available() probes the device.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: The standard route: build an experiment, QC, HVGs, PCA, neighbours, clusters, embedding, plots. It needs bixverse[embed,plots,sparse]. The blocks run top to bottom on synthetic data, so you can paste them as they are. The PBMC vignette does the same on real data and carries on to markers and annotation.

docs.title: An experiment
docs.text:
Synthetic counts with planted cell types, written into a new experiment directory:

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import polars as pl

import bixverse as bv
import bixverse.embed
from bixverse.params import SyntheticDataParams

sim = bv.io.generate_single_cell_test_data(
    SyntheticDataParams(n_cells=3000, n_genes=2000)
)

tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
sc = bv.io.load_csr(Path(tmp.name) / "demo", sim.counts.scipy_csr(), sim.obs, sim.var)
sc

load_csr takes a cells x genes CSR matrix plus obs and var as polars frames. Real data goes through bv.io.load_mtx, load_h5ad or load_tenx_h5 instead, and bv.io.download_pbmc3k() fetches PBMC3k to try them on. The result is the same: a directory holding the cell- and gene-major stores and a DuckDB with obs and var.

Back at it tomorrow? bv.io.save(sc) writes the cache next to the stores and bv.io.load_existing(directory) opens it again, ready to go.

sc.obs().head()
sc.var().head()

docs.title: Quality control
docs.text:
Gene set proportions land straight in obs. Here we take the first ten genes as the set; on real data you'd pass the mitochondrial and ribosomal gene ids.

var = sc.var()
gene_sets = {"set_a": var["gene_id"].head(10).to_list()}

bv.qc.gene_set_proportions(sc, gene_sets, streaming=False)

run_cell_qc does MAD-based outlier calls per metric and combines them:

qc_df = sc.obs(cols=["lib_size", "nnz", "set_a"])

qc = bv.qc.run_cell_qc(
    {
        "log10_lib_size": np.log10(qc_df["lib_size"].to_numpy()),
        "log10_nnz": np.log10(qc_df["nnz"].to_numpy()),
        "set_a": qc_df["set_a"].to_numpy(),
    },
    sc.cells_to_keep,
    directions={
        "log10_lib_size": "twosided",
        "log10_nnz": "twosided",
        "set_a": "above",
    },
    threshold=3.0,
)

print(f"{qc.combined.sum()} of {qc.combined.size} cells flagged")

bv.pl.violin_plot(qc)
plt.show()
bv.pl.joint_plot(qc)
plt.show()

Nothing is deleted. Store the flag in obs and tell the object which cells to keep. Every method from here on only sees those.

sc.add_obs(pl.DataFrame({"cell_idx": qc.cell_idx, "outlier": qc.combined}))
sc.set_cells_to_keep(qc.cell_idx[~qc.combined])
sc

docs.title: HVGs, PCA, neighbours, clusters
docs.text:
bv.pp.find_hvg(sc, hvg_no=500)
bv.pp.calculate_pca(sc, no_pcs=20, sparse_svd=True)
bv.graph.find_neighbours(sc)
bv.graph.find_clusters(sc, res=1.0, name="leiden_clusters")

HVGs, PCA and the kNN graph sit in the object's cache, and sc prints what's there and what has gone stale. Clusters are an obs column. On a real data set use hvg_no=2000 and no_pcs=30, and see clustering and annotation for bv.graph.fast_cluster on big data.

docs.title: Embedding and plots
docs.text:
UMAP and t-SNE come from manifolds-rs (the embed extra), the plots from matplotlib (the plots extra):

bv.embed.umap(sc)

bv.pl.embedding_plot(
    sc, "umap", "leiden_clusters", label_by="leiden_clusters", discrete=True
)
plt.show()

gene = sc.var()["gene_id"][0]
bv.pl.feature_plot(sc, [gene], "umap")
plt.show()

bv.embed.tsne(sc) is the t-SNE twin, and embedding_plot takes "tsne" the same way.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Markers with bv.de.find_all_markers, scType annotation, doublets, batch correction, metacells, ligand-receptor: the vignettes cover each. Start with PBMCs, design choices, I/O and visualisation. On a GPU, import bixverse_gpu as bvg and swap bv.pp.calculate_pca for bvg.pp.calculate_pca, likewise graph and embed.

docs.title: Loader
docs.text:
The cell-major store streams into minibatches for training. Open it with bv.CellReader and iterate:

reader = bv.CellReader(str(sc.cells_path))
loader = bv.CellLoader(reader, batch_size=256, layer="norm", seed=42)

for batch in loader:
    x = batch.scipy_csr()  # (256, n_genes) CSR
    break

A Batch carries raw, norm, indices, indptr, shape and cell_ids; the layer you didn't ask for is None. layer is "raw", "norm" or "both". norm is log1p(count / library_size * target_size) at float16 precision, so expect agreement with your own recomputation to about three decimal places.

Pass an index array to iterate a subset, and genes= (store gene indices, in the column order you want) to subset or reorder genes:

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
perm = rng.permutation(reader.total_cells)
n_train = int(0.8 * len(perm))

train = bv.CellLoader(reader, perm[:n_train], batch_size=256)
val = bv.CellLoader(reader, perm[n_train:], batch_size=256, shuffle=False)

Batches are sparse by default and you want it that way: a dense batch pays a zero-fill and a scatter over batch_size * n_genes floats however few counts it holds. Each pass reshuffles and spawns its own feeder thread; the seed is mixed with the epoch counter. Ctrl-C can't interrupt a batch mid-decode, because the GIL is released while the feeder works. For training scVI off the store, see scVI.

docs.title: scVI
docs.text:
bixverse.nn carries a barebone scVI (Lopez et al., Nature Methods, 2018) for batch correction. It trains straight off a bixverse store: counts stream through the Rust loader, so there's no AnnData, no Lightning and no registry in the way. Three backends with the same network on all of them: torch (cuda, mps or cpu), MLX on Apple Silicon and JAX (cpu or cuda).

pip install "bixverse[torch]"   # or bixverse[mlx] on Apple Silicon, bixverse[jax]

docs.title: Train and embed
docs.text:
You hand it the store, the cells to use, the genes to model and one batch label per cell. Indices are the store's own, 0-based.

import numpy as np
import bixverse.nn as bvnn

store = "counts_cells.bin"
cells = np.array([...])  # store cell indices, e.g. the QC survivors
hvg = np.array([...])  # store gene indices, e.g. 2000 HVGs
batch = np.array([...])  # one label per entry of `cells`

fit = bvnn.train_scvi(store, cells, hvg, batch, backend="torch", seed=42)
latent = bvnn.scvi_latent(fit, store, cells, batch)  # (n_cells, 10)

latent comes back in the order of cells, and is the posterior mean of z, same as scvi-tools' get_latent_representation(). Feed it to whatever builds your kNN graph.

Training shows a tqdm bar over the epochs with the current loss. verbose=2 also logs one line per epoch, verbose=False turns it all off.

Want a held-out score? Train on a subset of the cells and score the rest:

bvnn.scvi_elbo(fit, store, test_cells, test_batch)
# {'elbo': ..., 'reconstruction': ..., 'kl': ...}, means per cell

docs.title: What's in, what's out
docs.text:
The defaults are scvi-tools 1.5.1's SCVI plus its TrainingPlan: ZINB likelihood (NB via ScviParams(gene_likelihood="nb")), observed library size, gene-wise dispersion, one hidden layer of 128, a 10-d latent, batch one-hot into every decoder layer with the encoder blind to batch, Adam with lr 1e-3, eps 0.01 and weight decay 1e-6, batch size 128, KL warmup over 400 epochs and scvi-tools' epoch heuristic (min(round(20000 / n_cells * 400), 400)).

Not there, and not coming until something asks for it: Poisson and Gaussian likelihoods, learned library size, batch-, label- or cell-wise dispersion, extra covariates, labels (so no scANVI), minified data and scArches surgery.

Library size is the sum over the genes you pass, like scvi-tools on an HVG AnnData. A cell with no counts over those genes raises rather than training on log(0).

docs.title: How close is it to scvi-tools?
docs.text:
Two levels of check.

Same weights, same answer. The tests load a trained scvi-tools 1.5.1 module into ours, run both on one batch with z at the posterior mean, and compare. The encoder mean, reconstruction term and KL agree to rtol = 1e-5, for NB and ZINB. Our torch weights then go into the MLX model and agree to 1e-4 (MLX has no lgamma, so it uses a Lanczos approximation), and into the JAX model, which agrees to 1e-5, BatchNorm running statistics included.

Same training, same kind of result. Every arm trains on the same cells of the two PBMC batches from the bixverse batch correction vignette (6626 cells after QC, 2000 HVGs, 90/10 split, so 5963 train and 663 held out), 400 epochs, three seeds each, all in one sitting on an M1 Max:

arm device train, s held-out ELBO kBET accept iLISI Procrustes kNN Jaccard Leiden ARI scvi-tools SCVI cpu 260 769.2 0.684 1.480 0.489 0.084 0.741 scvi-tools SCVI mps 194 768.4 0.687 1.482 0.446 0.094 0.727 scvi-tools mlxSCVI gpu 124 0.846 1.605 0.526 0.082 0.724 bixverse torch cpu 202 768.8 0.689 1.486 0.469 0.088 0.718 bixverse torch mps 82 769.2 0.686 1.484 0.491 0.086 0.714 bixverse JAX cpu 106 768.3 0.694 1.491 0.475 0.087 0.721 bixverse MLX gpu 35 768.3 0.667 1.473 0.458 0.091 0.711 uncorrected PCA 0.013 1.014 Harmony 0.883 1.622

Means over three seeds. Held-out ELBO is the per-cell negative ELBO on the held-out cells, every arm scored by the same code (scvi-tools weights loaded into ours); its seed-to-seed range is up to about 2. kBET and iLISI come from bixverse's bv.integrate.calculate_integration_metrics and bv.integrate.calculate_lisi.

The last three columns compare each arm against scvi-tools on cpu: Procrustes disparity (0 is identical), the mean Jaccard of each cell's 15 nearest neighbours, and the ARI between Leiden clusterings, averaged over all pairs of seeds. VAE latents aren't identifiable, so two seeds of scvi-tools already disagree with each other, and the scvi-tools cpu row is exactly that: its own seed-to-seed spread. Ours sits inside it on every measure. A Procrustes disparity near 0.5 between two runs of the same code is also the reason a small Procrustes delta is the wrong thing to ask for.

On speed: MLX is the crown on Apple Silicon. torch on MPS beats scvi-tools on MPS by more than 2x; the network is the same, so the gap sits outside the maths, mostly torch.distributions argument checks that stall the GPU queue every step, plus Lightning's per-step bookkeeping. Data loading costs the same on both sides. No GPU? Take JAX: it's almost twice as fast as torch on the same CPU, for the same ELBO. That was scvi-tools' original pitch for JaxSCVI back in 0.15, and it still holds for this network.

scvi-tools' own mlxSCVI is a different network (two hidden layers, BatchNorm momentum 0.9, NB or Poisson only), so it's not a port of SCVI and has no held-out ELBO here. It integrates harder on these two batches, closer to Harmony than to SCVI.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• scvi-tools' accelerator="auto" ignores MPS. Ask for "mps" explicitly if you benchmark against it.
  • The MLX backend compiles its training step with mx.compile. On this data that took 400 epochs from 82 s to 50 s.
  • torch.compile isn't used. On MPS it cut compute from 0.175 s to 0.136 s per epoch but costs about 5 s up front, and the inductor backend there is still experimental.
  • JAX on Apple's GPU goes through the jax-metal plugin, which only runs pinned to jax 0.5.0. It trains, but took about 180 s on this data, slower than JAX on CPU, so it isn't supported. Use MLX there.
  • The JAX training step compiles twice per fit, once for the full batch size and once for the short final batch.
  • There's no torch DataLoader in the loop: the Rust feeder thread already decodes ahead of the training step.

docs.title: Annotation
docs.text:
Cell type annotation with ScType and reference mapping with Symphony.

ScType scores every cell against marker gene sets and calls a type per cell, optionally per cluster. Symphony builds a Harmony-corrected reference from an annotated experiment, maps a query into its embedding and transfers the labels by kNN vote. Start with prepare_cell_markers, calc_sc_type_scores and assign_sc_type for ScType, build_symphony_ref, map_symphony_query and transfer_labels_symphony for Symphony.

What lands where. The ScType functions leave the experiment alone and return frozen records (ScTypeResults, ScTypeCellResults); put a call into obs yourself. map_symphony_query writes the query embeddings to query.cache.embeddings as "symphony" (corrected), "symphony_pca" (projected) and "symphony_r" (soft cluster assignments). transfer_labels_symphony writes predicted_<column> and confidence_<column> to the query's obs and returns them. build_symphony_ref and add_symphony_labels return a SymphonyReference and touch neither experiment. A reference is immutable: adding labels gives you a new one. All functions take a SingleCells.

ScType wants markers as a frame of cell_type and gene_id, in the id type of the experiment, and scores the kept cells. The neighbour graph smooths the scores, so run bv.graph.find_neighbours first; clusters from bv.graph.find_clusters add a per cluster call.

import polars as pl

genes = sc.gene_ids().tolist()
marker_df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "cell_type": ["type_1"] * 10 + ["type_2"] * 10 + ["type_3"] * 10,
        "gene_id": genes[:30],
    }
)
markers = bv.annotate.prepare_cell_markers(sc, marker_df)
scores = bv.annotate.calc_sc_type_scores(sc, markers)
calls = bv.annotate.assign_sc_type(sc, scores, cluster_col="leiden_clustering")
sc.add_obs(pl.DataFrame({"cell_idx": sc.cells_to_keep, "sc_type": calls.hybrid}))

Symphony needs the reference's HVGs, so run bv.pp.find_hvg on it first and hand sc.map.hvg over. Genes match by id; a reference HVG missing from the query becomes a zero column:

ref = bv.annotate.build_symphony_ref(
    sc, "sample_id", sc.map.hvg, label_columns=["cell_grp"]
)
bv.annotate.map_symphony_query(ref, query, batch_column="sample_id")
pred = bv.annotate.transfer_labels_symphony(ref, query, "cell_grp")

Gotchas. Every index is 0-based: marker genes, HVGs and cluster ids. cluster_col of assign_sc_type has to be a non-negative integer obs column with a value for every scored cell, which is what find_clusters writes. Without a neighbour graph assign_sc_type warns and scores without smoothing. calls.hybrid is None unless you gave a cluster_col; calls.assignments is the per cell call, null where the cell is Unknown. Labels are stored in a reference in cells_to_keep order, so add_symphony_labels needs the cell set the reference was built on. transfer_labels_symphony raises on a query that has no current "symphony" embedding: map again after the cell filter moves. save_symphony_ref and load_symphony_ref use one .npz file.

Worked through in Clustering, cell type annotation and reference mapping.

docs.title: Symphony reference
docs.text:
Cell type annotation with ScType and reference mapping with Symphony.

ScType scores every cell against marker gene sets and calls a type per cell, optionally per cluster. Symphony builds a Harmony-corrected reference from an annotated experiment, maps a query into its embedding and transfers the labels by kNN vote. Start with prepare_cell_markers, calc_sc_type_scores and assign_sc_type for ScType, build_symphony_ref, map_symphony_query and transfer_labels_symphony for Symphony.

What lands where. The ScType functions leave the experiment alone and return frozen records (ScTypeResults, ScTypeCellResults); put a call into obs yourself. map_symphony_query writes the query embeddings to query.cache.embeddings as "symphony" (corrected), "symphony_pca" (projected) and "symphony_r" (soft cluster assignments). transfer_labels_symphony writes predicted_<column> and confidence_<column> to the query's obs and returns them. build_symphony_ref and add_symphony_labels return a SymphonyReference and touch neither experiment. A reference is immutable: adding labels gives you a new one. All functions take a SingleCells.

ScType wants markers as a frame of cell_type and gene_id, in the id type of the experiment, and scores the kept cells. The neighbour graph smooths the scores, so run bv.graph.find_neighbours first; clusters from bv.graph.find_clusters add a per cluster call.

import polars as pl

genes = sc.gene_ids().tolist()
marker_df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "cell_type": ["type_1"] * 10 + ["type_2"] * 10 + ["type_3"] * 10,
        "gene_id": genes[:30],
    }
)
markers = bv.annotate.prepare_cell_markers(sc, marker_df)
scores = bv.annotate.calc_sc_type_scores(sc, markers)
calls = bv.annotate.assign_sc_type(sc, scores, cluster_col="leiden_clustering")
sc.add_obs(pl.DataFrame({"cell_idx": sc.cells_to_keep, "sc_type": calls.hybrid}))

Symphony needs the reference's HVGs, so run bv.pp.find_hvg on it first and hand sc.map.hvg over. Genes match by id; a reference HVG missing from the query becomes a zero column:

ref = bv.annotate.build_symphony_ref(
    sc, "sample_id", sc.map.hvg, label_columns=["cell_grp"]
)
bv.annotate.map_symphony_query(ref, query, batch_column="sample_id")
pred = bv.annotate.transfer_labels_symphony(ref, query, "cell_grp")

Gotchas. Every index is 0-based: marker genes, HVGs and cluster ids. cluster_col of assign_sc_type has to be a non-negative integer obs column with a value for every scored cell, which is what find_clusters writes. Without a neighbour graph assign_sc_type warns and scores without smoothing. calls.hybrid is None unless you gave a cluster_col; calls.assignments is the per cell call, null where the cell is Unknown. Labels are stored in a reference in cells_to_keep order, so add_symphony_labels needs the cell set the reference was built on. transfer_labels_symphony raises on a query that has no current "symphony" embedding: map again after the cell filter moves. save_symphony_ref and load_symphony_ref use one .npz file.

docs.title: Core
docs.text:
The experiment classes and the objects they hand around.

Single-cell streaming for Python, in Rust.

Opens a bixverse binary sparse store and yields minibatches fast enough to keep a GPU training loop fed. The decode never leaves Rust: a feeder thread decompresses and materialises batches ahead of the consumer, releasing the GIL while it works.

>>> import bixverse as bv
>>> reader = bv.CellReader("counts.bin")
>>> loader = bv.CellLoader(reader, batch_size=256, layer="norm")
>>> for batch in loader:
...     x = batch.scipy_csr()

Batches are sparse CSR by default. Pass sparse=False for a dense (batch_size, n_genes) array, and expect it to cost a zero-fill and a scatter over every gene whether or not it holds a count.

docs.title: Differential expression and abundance
docs.text:
Marker genes, donor-aware differential expression and differential abundance.

Three jobs. Markers: Wilcoxon between two groups (find_markers), one-vs-rest for every group of a column (find_all_markers), or markers that hold up against every rival group separately (find_specific_markers). Expression with donor structure: pseudobulk edgeR (get_pseudobulked, pseudobulk_dge, run_edger_ql) or the mixed model nebula. Abundance: Milo neighbourhoods (get_milor_abundances, test_nhoods, add_nhoods_info) and meld densities. Start with find_all_markers to look at clusters, pseudobulk_dge or nebula to compare conditions across donors.

What lands where. Nothing here writes to obs, var or the cache. The marker tests and pseudobulk_dge return polars frames; find_specific_markers, nebula, get_milor_abundances and meld return frozen records (ScSpecificMarkers, ScNebula, MiloR, MeldRes) with getters for their tables. test_nhoods and add_nhoods_info hand back a new MiloR carrying nhoods_info.

Object types. The marker functions, get_pseudobulked, pseudobulk_dge and nebula take a SingleCells or a SingleCellsSubset, so a per cell type comparison is a subset away. get_milor_abundances and meld take a SingleCells only.

markers = bv.de.find_all_markers(sc, "cell_grp")
top = markers.filter(markers["fdr"] < 0.05)

Condition across donors, one pseudobulk sample per donor. cell_list maps the sample names to their cells and the rows of the design follow its order:

import polars as pl

obs = sc.obs(filtered=True)
cell_list = {
    s: obs.filter(obs["sample_id"] == s)["cell_id"].to_list()
    for s in obs["sample_id"].unique().sort()
}
design = pl.DataFrame(
    {"(Intercept)": [1.0] * 6, "stim": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]}
)
pb_res = bv.de.pseudobulk_dge(sc, cell_list, design, coef="stim")

Milo needs a PCA and the kNN over it, and the sample column of obs. The design frame has one row per sample:

bv.pp.find_hvg(sc, hvg_no=500)
bv.pp.calculate_pca(sc, no_pcs=20)
bv.graph.find_neighbours(sc)

design_df = sc.obs().select("sample_id", "condition").unique().sort("sample_id")
milo = bv.de.get_milor_abundances(sc, "sample_id")
milo = bv.de.test_nhoods(milo, "~ condition", design_df)
da = bv.de.get_differential_abundance_res(milo)

Gotchas. Designs are additive formulas over a frame, "~ condition + age": numeric columns as they are, everything else treatment coded against its first (sorted) level and named <column><level>. Interactions and transformations are not parsed. coef takes a 0-based design column or its name, and the last column is tested if you give neither. Every index is 0-based, Milo's Nhood included. get_milor_abundances and meld raise on a stale embedding or kNN, so rerun those after the cell filter moves, and they warn and return None without a kNN. nebula costs milliseconds to seconds per gene: hand genes_to_use the HVGs or a candidate set. run_edger_ql wants raw counts and a design with an intercept and at least one more column.

Worked through in Differential expression with donor structure and Differential abundance with Milo and MELD.

docs.title: Pseudobulk edgeR
docs.text:
Marker genes, donor-aware differential expression and differential abundance.

Three jobs. Markers: Wilcoxon between two groups (find_markers), one-vs-rest for every group of a column (find_all_markers), or markers that hold up against every rival group separately (find_specific_markers). Expression with donor structure: pseudobulk edgeR (get_pseudobulked, pseudobulk_dge, run_edger_ql) or the mixed model nebula. Abundance: Milo neighbourhoods (get_milor_abundances, test_nhoods, add_nhoods_info) and meld densities. Start with find_all_markers to look at clusters, pseudobulk_dge or nebula to compare conditions across donors.

What lands where. Nothing here writes to obs, var or the cache. The marker tests and pseudobulk_dge return polars frames; find_specific_markers, nebula, get_milor_abundances and meld return frozen records (ScSpecificMarkers, ScNebula, MiloR, MeldRes) with getters for their tables. test_nhoods and add_nhoods_info hand back a new MiloR carrying nhoods_info.

Object types. The marker functions, get_pseudobulked, pseudobulk_dge and nebula take a SingleCells or a SingleCellsSubset, so a per cell type comparison is a subset away. get_milor_abundances and meld take a SingleCells only.

markers = bv.de.find_all_markers(sc, "cell_grp")
top = markers.filter(markers["fdr"] < 0.05)

Condition across donors, one pseudobulk sample per donor. cell_list maps the sample names to their cells and the rows of the design follow its order:

import polars as pl

obs = sc.obs(filtered=True)
cell_list = {
    s: obs.filter(obs["sample_id"] == s)["cell_id"].to_list()
    for s in obs["sample_id"].unique().sort()
}
design = pl.DataFrame(
    {"(Intercept)": [1.0] * 6, "stim": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]}
)
pb_res = bv.de.pseudobulk_dge(sc, cell_list, design, coef="stim")

Milo needs a PCA and the kNN over it, and the sample column of obs. The design frame has one row per sample:

bv.pp.find_hvg(sc, hvg_no=500)
bv.pp.calculate_pca(sc, no_pcs=20)
bv.graph.find_neighbours(sc)

design_df = sc.obs().select("sample_id", "condition").unique().sort("sample_id")
milo = bv.de.get_milor_abundances(sc, "sample_id")
milo = bv.de.test_nhoods(milo, "~ condition", design_df)
da = bv.de.get_differential_abundance_res(milo)

Gotchas. Designs are additive formulas over a frame, "~ condition + age": numeric columns as they are, everything else treatment coded against its first (sorted) level and named <column><level>. Interactions and transformations are not parsed. coef takes a 0-based design column or its name, and the last column is tested if you give neither. Every index is 0-based, Milo's Nhood included. get_milor_abundances and meld raise on a stale embedding or kNN, so rerun those after the cell filter moves, and they warn and return None without a kNN. nebula costs milliseconds to seconds per gene: hand genes_to_use the HVGs or a candidate set. run_edger_ql wants raw counts and a design with an intercept and at least one more column.

docs.text:
nebula(
    sc: ScOrScSubset,
    subject_col: str,
    design: str,
    *,
    coef: int | str | None = None,
    contrast: ndarray | Sequence[float] | None = None,
    genes_to_use: Selection | None = None,
    cells_to_use: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    offset: ndarray | Sequence[float] | None = None,
    nebula_params: NebulaParams | None = None,
    verbose: Verbose = True,
) -> ScNebula

NEBULA's negative binomial gamma mixed model.

The variance splits into a subject-level random effect and a cell-level overdispersion, so the donor structure is modelled rather than ignored. Genes stream through in batches, which is exact. A fit takes milliseconds to seconds per gene, so restrict genes_to_use to the HVGs or a candidate set.

Name Type Description Default sc ScOrScSubset

The experiment.

required subject_col str

obs column with the subject (donor), the random effect.

required design str

Formula over obs, e.g. "~ condition + age".

required coef int | str | None

The coefficient the Wald test reports, a 0-based design column or its name. None takes the last column.

None contrast ndarray | Sequence[float] | None

One weight per design column. Exclusive with coef.

None genes_to_use Selection | None

0-based gene indices or ids. None fits every gene.

None cells_to_use Sequence[str] | None

Cell ids to fit. None takes the kept cells; ids that are not kept warn and drop.

None offset ndarray | Sequence[float] | None

Strictly positive scaling per cell, aligned to the cells that survive the design. None uses the library sizes.

None nebula_params NebulaParams | None

The parameters. None uses the defaults.

None verbose Verbose

0 (False) silent, 1 (True) progress, 2 extra detail where the method has it.

True

The ScNebula.

Type Description ValueError

docs.title: MELD
docs.text:
Marker genes, donor-aware differential expression and differential abundance.

Three jobs. Markers: Wilcoxon between two groups (find_markers), one-vs-rest for every group of a column (find_all_markers), or markers that hold up against every rival group separately (find_specific_markers). Expression with donor structure: pseudobulk edgeR (get_pseudobulked, pseudobulk_dge, run_edger_ql) or the mixed model nebula. Abundance: Milo neighbourhoods (get_milor_abundances, test_nhoods, add_nhoods_info) and meld densities. Start with find_all_markers to look at clusters, pseudobulk_dge or nebula to compare conditions across donors.

What lands where. Nothing here writes to obs, var or the cache. The marker tests and pseudobulk_dge return polars frames; find_specific_markers, nebula, get_milor_abundances and meld return frozen records (ScSpecificMarkers, ScNebula, MiloR, MeldRes) with getters for their tables. test_nhoods and add_nhoods_info hand back a new MiloR carrying nhoods_info.

Object types. The marker functions, get_pseudobulked, pseudobulk_dge and nebula take a SingleCells or a SingleCellsSubset, so a per cell type comparison is a subset away. get_milor_abundances and meld take a SingleCells only.

markers = bv.de.find_all_markers(sc, "cell_grp")
top = markers.filter(markers["fdr"] < 0.05)

Condition across donors, one pseudobulk sample per donor. cell_list maps the sample names to their cells and the rows of the design follow its order:

import polars as pl

obs = sc.obs(filtered=True)
cell_list = {
    s: obs.filter(obs["sample_id"] == s)["cell_id"].to_list()
    for s in obs["sample_id"].unique().sort()
}
design = pl.DataFrame(
    {"(Intercept)": [1.0] * 6, "stim": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]}
)
pb_res = bv.de.pseudobulk_dge(sc, cell_list, design, coef="stim")

Milo needs a PCA and the kNN over it, and the sample column of obs. The design frame has one row per sample:

bv.pp.find_hvg(sc, hvg_no=500)
bv.pp.calculate_pca(sc, no_pcs=20)
bv.graph.find_neighbours(sc)

design_df = sc.obs().select("sample_id", "condition").unique().sort("sample_id")
milo = bv.de.get_milor_abundances(sc, "sample_id")
milo = bv.de.test_nhoods(milo, "~ condition", design_df)
da = bv.de.get_differential_abundance_res(milo)

Gotchas. Designs are additive formulas over a frame, "~ condition + age": numeric columns as they are, everything else treatment coded against its first (sorted) level and named <column><level>. Interactions and transformations are not parsed. coef takes a 0-based design column or its name, and the last column is tested if you give neither. Every index is 0-based, Milo's Nhood included. get_milor_abundances and meld raise on a stale embedding or kNN, so rerun those after the cell filter moves, and they warn and return None without a kNN. nebula costs milliseconds to seconds per gene: hand genes_to_use the HVGs or a candidate set. run_edger_ql wants raw counts and a design with an intercept and at least one more column.

docs.title: DIALOGUE
docs.text:
DIALOGUE: multicellular programmes, genes that are cell type specific but whose activity covaries across the samples the cell types share.

One function does the work. dialogue takes an experiment, the obs columns that hold the cell types and the samples, and a per-cell-type feature frame, and returns a DialogueResult. Read it with get_results (the programme table) or straight off its fields: signatures for the permissive and strict gene lists, scores for the per-cell programme scores, refit_fidelity for how well each cell type's score survived the final refit. Programmes are 0-based: mcp_00 is programme 0.

What lands where. Nothing is written to the experiment. The result is returned, and the run reads the normalised layer of the kept cells only. SingleCells, SingleCellsSubset and MetaCells are all accepted; for meta cells the ids are meta_cell_id and you build them within samples, or a meta cell has no well-defined sample.

Features are yours to make. Per cell type, a frame of cell_id plus at least two numeric columns, rows matched to cells by id. Compute them within the cell type (subset, find_hvg, calculate_pca): slicing a global PCA hands every cell type the same axis. Genes for the signatures default to the HVGs, so run bv.pp.find_hvg first or pass gene_ids.

sim = bv.io.generate_dialogue_test_data()
sc = bv.io.load_csr("dialogue_demo", sim.counts.scipy_csr(), sim.obs, sim.var)
bv.pp.find_hvg(sc, hvg_no=200)

res = bv.dialogue.dialogue(
    sc,
    "cell_grp",
    "sample_id",
    sim.features,
    pmd_params=bv.params.DialoguePmdParams(k=2, n_permutations=100),
)
bv.dialogue.get_results(res)
res.signatures.filter(res.signatures["list"] == "strict")

Gotchas. The design decides whether it runs at all: at least two cell types and five samples present in every one of them, with enough cells per sample per cell type to clear abn_c. It errors below that. k is the number of programmes you ask for, with no sweep to pick it, and n_permutations sets the floor of the empirical p-value. Without quality_col the cell quality covariate is the z-scored log library size, which needs lib_size in obs.

References: Jerby-Arnon & Regev, Nat. Biotechnol., 2022.

Worked through in Multicellular programmes with DIALOGUE.

docs.title: dialogue
docs.text:
dialogue(
    sc: ScOrMc,
    cell_type_col: str,
    sample_col: str,
    features: Mapping[str, DataFrame],
    *,
    quality_col: str | None = None,
    gene_ids: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    pmd_params: DialoguePmdParams | None = None,
    hlm_params: DialogueHlmParams | None = None,
    refine_params: DialogueRefineParams | None = None,
    verbose: Verbose = True,
) -> DialogueResult

Multicellular programmes.

Three stages. Each cell type's features are collapsed to one row per sample and put through a sparse multi-CCA, giving every programme a weight vector per cell type plus a provisional gene signature. For every ordered pair of cell types and every candidate gene, a mixed model asks whether a cell's programme score tracks the partner cell type's expression of that gene in the same sample. The partners are then meta-analysed and the scores refit onto the surviving genes by non-negative least squares. Reads the normalised counts only.

The method needs at least two cell types, five samples present in every one of them, and enough cells per sample per cell type to clear abn_c. For meta cells, build them within samples, or the sample of a meta cell is not well-defined.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default sc ScOrMc

The kept cells of the experiment, a subset, or meta cells.

required cell_type_col str

obs column with the cell type labels.

required sample_col str

obs column with the sample labels; the random intercept of stage two is over these.

required features Mapping[str, DataFrame]

Per analysed cell type (the keys, in order) a frame of cell_id (meta_cell_id for meta cells) plus at least two numeric feature columns covering that cell type's cells.

required quality_col str | None

obs column with the cell quality covariate. None uses the z-scored log1p library size (lib_size in obs; the summed raw counts for meta cells).

None gene_ids Sequence[str] | None

Genes to build the signatures from. None uses the HVGs.

None pmd_params DialoguePmdParams | None

Stage one parameters. None uses the defaults.

None hlm_params DialogueHlmParams | None

Stage two parameters. None uses the defaults.

None refine_params DialogueRefineParams | None

Stage three parameters. None uses the defaults.

None verbose Verbose

0 (False) silent, 1 (True) progress, 2 extra detail where the method has it.

True

Returns:

Type Description DialogueResult

The DialogueResult.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

On a design DIALOGUE cannot run on, malformed features, or no genes.

Examples:

>>> res = bv.dialogue.dialogue(
...     sc,
...     "cell_grp",
...     "sample_id",
...     features,
...     pmd_params=bv.params.DialoguePmdParams(k=2, n_permutations=100),
... )
>>> res = bv.dialogue.dialogue(
...     sc, "cell_grp", "sample_id", features, quality_col="cell_quality"
... )

Jerby-Arnon & Regev, Nat. Biotechnol., 2022.

docs.title: Doublets and ambient RNA
docs.text:
Doublet callers, empty-droplet calls and CellSweep ambient RNA removal.

Three callers find doublets from the counts: scrublet, doublet_detection_boost and scdblfinder. Run one, turn the result into an obs frame with get_data and add it. cellsweep is a separate job: it removes ambient and bulk contamination from a raw experiment that still holds its empty droplets, and uses infer_empty_droplets to find them.

What lands where. The callers leave the experiment alone and return a frozen record (ScrubletRes, BoostRes, ScDblFinderRes). get_data turns a record into a frame with a 0-based cell_idx for sc.add_obs. call_doublets_manual re-calls a Scrublet result at a threshold of your choosing and returns a new record. get_feature_mat and get_scores read the classifier output of an scDblFinder record. infer_empty_droplets returns a boolean array. cellsweep writes a new experiment into the directory you give it and returns it, with cellsweep_alpha, cellsweep_z, cellsweep_beta, cellsweep_ll and cellsweep_converged in obs and cellsweep_ambient in var. The input stays as it was.

Object types. All functions take a SingleCells. The callers run on the kept cells unless you hand them cells_to_use.

res = bv.doublets.scrublet(sc, group_by="sample_id")
sc.add_obs(bv.doublets.get_data(res))
sc.obs()[["doublet", "doublet_score"]].head()

With group_by every method runs once per group, and per-group scalars such as threshold become {group: value} dicts. Doublets form inside a droplet emulsion, so group by the sample or the lane, never across them. A group below 50 cells is an error, below 500 a warning.

Gotchas. get_data names its columns after the caller: Scrublet and Boost both write doublet and doublet_score, so adding the second replaces the first. Take one result at a time, or rename the columns before add_obs. call_doublets_manual only takes Scrublet results; on a grouped one it re-calls a single group (for_sample, else the first). cellsweep runs after annotation and wants the empty droplets in the object, so ingest with MinQualityParams(min_unique_genes=0, min_lib_size=0, min_cells=0); with the default freeze_ambient_profile it refuses an object whose smallest library size is above 100. Barcodes that are neither empty nor annotated and kept are left out of the fit and the output.

Worked through in Doublet detection with bixverse and Ambient RNA removal with CellSweep.

docs.text:
Doublet callers, empty-droplet calls and CellSweep ambient RNA removal.

Three callers find doublets from the counts: scrublet, doublet_detection_boost and scdblfinder. Run one, turn the result into an obs frame with get_data and add it. cellsweep is a separate job: it removes ambient and bulk contamination from a raw experiment that still holds its empty droplets, and uses infer_empty_droplets to find them.

What lands where. The callers leave the experiment alone and return a frozen record (ScrubletRes, BoostRes, ScDblFinderRes). get_data turns a record into a frame with a 0-based cell_idx for sc.add_obs. call_doublets_manual re-calls a Scrublet result at a threshold of your choosing and returns a new record. get_feature_mat and get_scores read the classifier output of an scDblFinder record. infer_empty_droplets returns a boolean array. cellsweep writes a new experiment into the directory you give it and returns it, with cellsweep_alpha, cellsweep_z, cellsweep_beta, cellsweep_ll and cellsweep_converged in obs and cellsweep_ambient in var. The input stays as it was.

Object types. All functions take a SingleCells. The callers run on the kept cells unless you hand them cells_to_use.

res = bv.doublets.scrublet(sc, group_by="sample_id")
sc.add_obs(bv.doublets.get_data(res))
sc.obs()[["doublet", "doublet_score"]].head()

With group_by every method runs once per group, and per-group scalars such as threshold become {group: value} dicts. Doublets form inside a droplet emulsion, so group by the sample or the lane, never across them. A group below 50 cells is an error, below 500 a warning.

Gotchas. get_data names its columns after the caller: Scrublet and Boost both write doublet and doublet_score, so adding the second replaces the first.     directory: Path | str,
    sc: SingleCells,

docs.title: Embeddings
docs.text:
2D embeddings: UMAP, densMAP, t-SNE, den-SNE, PHATE and ForceAtlas2.

Start with umap on the neighbours from bv.graph.find_neighbours. Every function reads a cached embedding (the PCA by default), fits, and writes the coordinates to sc.cache.embeddings under slot_name ("umap", "densmap", "tsne", "densne", "phate", "fa2"), stamped as derived from the input embedding and, when the cached kNN fed it, from the kNN. Nothing is returned. All of them take a SingleCells, SingleCellsSubset or MetaCells; on a SingleCellsMultiModal, modality="wnn" takes the RNA embedding and the WNN kNN.

The numerics come from the manifolds-rs wheel, an optional extra: pip install bixverse[embed]. Importing bv.embed without it raises.

Parameters are the manifolds_rs estimators themselves. The *_defaults() builders return one set to the bixverse defaults, which differ from the estimators' own in places (t-SNE perplexity is 10, not 30). Tweak one with set_params and hand it over as params.

bv.graph.find_neighbours(sc)
bv.embed.umap(sc)
bv.embed.tsne(sc, params=bv.embed.tsne_defaults().set_params(perplexity=20.0))
umap_xy = sc.cache.embeddings["umap"]

UMAP and densMAP take optimiser="sgd_parallel", umap-learn's SGD run lock-free over all threads (Hogwild!). It is fast and not reproducible: the same seed gives a different embedding each run. n_epochs defaults to None, which is 500, or 200 for the SGD optimisers above 10,000 cells.

Gotchas. With use_knn=True (the default for UMAP, densMAP and ForceAtlas2) the cached kNN is reused and the neighbour search settings in params don't apply. A graph wider than n_neighbors is cut to it, with a warning on stderr; a narrower one is used as it is. With no kNN cached you get a warning and a fresh search. t-SNE, den-SNE and PHATE search afresh unless you ask for the cached kNN; if you do, keep its k near three times the perplexity for t-SNE, and at 6k + 5 (35 by default) for PHATE. A stale input raises, and so does a slot_name that is reserved (the PCA, kNN and so on). ForceAtlas2 lays out the fuzzy kNN graph; laying out a graph you supply is not possible.

Worked through in Analysing PBMCs with bixverse.

docs.title: Neighbours and clusters
docs.text:
kNN search, the neighbour graph and clustering.

Start with find_neighbours on a PCA (or any cached embedding), then find_clusters for Leiden or Louvain on the resulting graph. The UMAP and the other embeddings in bv.embed, and the integration metrics in bv.integrate, read the same kNN.

What lands where. find_neighbours writes the kNN to sc.cache.knn and its symmetrised graph to sc.cache.connectivities, both stamped, so sc prints what has gone stale. find_clusters writes the labels to an obs column, 0-based with 0 the largest community. generate_knn, fast_cluster, calc_knn_metrics and get_connectivities return their result and leave the experiment alone. SingleCells works everywhere. SingleCellsSubset is accepted by all but generate_knn, and its labels go to the subset's obs. find_neighbours, find_clusters and get_connectivities also take MetaCells, and on a SingleCellsMultiModal they reach the ADT and WNN graphs through modality.

bv.graph.find_neighbours(sc, neighbours_params=bv.params.NeighboursParams(k=15))
bv.graph.find_clusters(sc, res=1.0, name="leiden_clustering")

Big data, or only want rough labels? fast_cluster coarsens with k-means, clusters the centroids and hands each cell the label of its centroid. With several seeds it also reports how stable the labels are. To check an approximate index, build an exact generate_knn as the reference and compare with calc_knn_metrics.

Gotchas. The embedding must exist and be fresh: find_neighbours raises on a stale PCA and warns and returns if the embedding is absent. find_clusters raises if the graph is stale or does not cover the kept cells, so rebuild the neighbours after moving the cell filter. Resolutions don't carry over between knn_sym choices ("snn", "umap", "knn"): retune res when you switch. bv.integrate.bbknn overwrites the kNN and the graph. The graph is the symmetric CSR in sc.cache.connectivities; get_connectivities(sc).scipy_csr() takes it to scipy, igraph or networkx.

Worked through in KNN searches for single cell and Clustering, cell type annotation and reference mapping.

docs.title: kNN searches and their quality
docs.text:
kNN search, the neighbour graph and clustering.

Start with find_neighbours on a PCA (or any cached embedding), then find_clusters for Leiden or Louvain on the resulting graph. The UMAP and the other embeddings in bv.embed, and the integration metrics in bv.integrate, read the same kNN.

What lands where. find_neighbours writes the kNN to sc.cache.knn and its symmetrised graph to sc.cache.connectivities, both stamped, so sc prints what has gone stale. find_clusters writes the labels to an obs column, 0-based with 0 the largest community. generate_knn, fast_cluster, calc_knn_metrics and get_connectivities return their result and leave the experiment alone. SingleCells works everywhere. SingleCellsSubset is accepted by all but generate_knn, and its labels go to the subset's obs. find_neighbours, find_clusters and get_connectivities also take MetaCells, and on a SingleCellsMultiModal they reach the ADT and WNN graphs through modality.

bv.graph.find_neighbours(sc, neighbours_params=bv.params.NeighboursParams(k=15))
bv.graph.find_clusters(sc, res=1.0, name="leiden_clustering")

Big data, or only want rough labels? fast_cluster coarsens with k-means, clusters the centroids and hands each cell the label of its centroid. With several seeds it also reports how stable the labels are. To check an approximate index, build an exact generate_knn as the reference and compare with calc_knn_metrics.

Gotchas. The embedding must exist and be fresh: find_neighbours raises on a stale PCA and warns and returns if the embedding is absent. find_clusters raises if the graph is stale or does not cover the kept cells, so rebuild the neighbours after moving the cell filter. Resolutions don't carry over between knn_sym choices ("snn", "umap", "knn"): retune res when you switch. bv.integrate.bbknn overwrites the kNN and the graph. The graph is the symmetric CSR in sc.cache.connectivities; get_connectivities(sc).scipy_csr() takes it to scipy, igraph or networkx.

docs.title: Batch correction
docs.text:
Batch correction and integration metrics.

Pick a correction, then check it. harmony (v2) and harmony_v1 (the original) correct the cached PCA. fast_mnn, seurat_cca and seurat_rpca work from the counts of the batch-aware HVGs, so run bv.pp.find_hvg_batch_aware first and hand them its hvg_gene_idx. bbknn skips the embedding and builds a batch-balanced kNN instead. The calculate_* functions score the result, and calculate_integration_metrics runs the lot and returns one row.

What lands where. Harmony, fastMNN, CCA and rPCA write a corrected embedding to sc.cache.embeddings under "harmony", "harmony_v1", "mnn", "cca" and "rpca". bbknn writes sc.cache.knn and sc.cache.connectivities, replacing what is there. All are stamped. The metrics return records (or a table) and leave the experiment alone. Everything takes a SingleCells or SingleCellsSubset except seurat_cca and seurat_rpca, which want a SingleCells. The batch labels are an obs column named by batch_column; its levels are sorted, an Enum keeps its own order.

bv.pp.find_hvg(sc, hvg_no=2000)
bv.pp.calculate_pca(sc, no_pcs=30)
bv.integrate.harmony(sc, "batch_index")
bv.graph.find_neighbours(sc, embd_to_use="harmony")
metrics = bv.integrate.calculate_integration_metrics(
    sc, "batch_index", cell_type_column="cell_grp", embd_to_use="harmony"
)

Gotchas. The kNN metrics (calculate_kbet, calculate_lisi, calculate_graph_connectivity) read the cached kNN, so rebuild the neighbours on the corrected embedding before scoring it; on a stale kNN they warn, on one that covers other cells they raise. The silhouette widths are O(n^2) and subsample to max_cells (5000). calculate_pcr compares a corrected embedding with the PCA, so it needs both. For bbknn there is no embedding: pass embd_to_use=None to calculate_integration_metrics, and the metrics that need one come back null. A single batch warns and returns without doing anything, bar fast_mnn, which raises. seurat_cca and seurat_rpca with use_precomputed_pca=True still need the gene loadings, so they save less than fastMNN does.

Worked through in Batch correction with bixverse.

Harmony, fastMNN, CCA and rPCA write a corrected embedding to sc.cache.embeddings under "harmony", "harmony_v1", "mnn", "cca" and "rpca". bbknn writes sc.cache.knn and sc.cache.connectivities, replacing what is there. All are stamped. The metrics return records (or a table) and leave the experiment alone. Everything takes a SingleCells or SingleCellsSubset except seurat_cca and seurat_rpca, which want a SingleCells. The batch labels are an obs column named by batch_column; its levels are sorted, an Enum keeps its own order.

bv.pp.find_hvg(sc, hvg_no=2000)
bv.pp.calculate_pca(sc, no_pcs=30)
bv.integrate.harmony(sc, "batch_index")
bv.graph.find_neighbours(sc, embd_to_use="harmony")
metrics = bv.integrate.calculate_integration_metrics(
    sc, "batch_index", cell_type_column="cell_grp", embd_to_use="harmony"
)

Gotchas. The kNN metrics (calculate_kbet, calculate_lisi, calculate_graph_connectivity) read the cached kNN, so rebuild the neighbours on the corrected embedding before scoring it; on a stale kNN they warn, on one that covers other cells they raise. The silhouette widths are O(n^2) and subsample to max_cells (5000). calculate_pcr compares a corrected embedding with the PCA, so it needs both. For bbknn there is no embedding: pass embd_to_use=None to calculate_integration_metrics, and the metrics that need one come back null. A single batch warns and returns without doing anything, bar fast_mnn, which raises. seurat_cca and seurat_rpca with use_precomputed_pca=True still need the gene loadings, so they save less than fastMNN does.

docs.title: Input and output
docs.text:
Getting counts into an experiment directory, and back out.

Every loader takes the directory to create and returns the opened SingleCells. Pick the one for your format: load_csr for counts already in memory, load_h5ad, load_tenx_h5 or load_mtx for files, and the load_multi_* twins for several files in one go. After the first load you only need load_existing.

What a load does. It applies the cell and gene QC of MinQualityParams (by default at least 100 genes, 250 counts per cell and 10 cells per gene), so dropped cells and genes never enter the store. It then writes the cell-major and gene-major stores and loads obs and var into the DuckDB, adding nnz and lib_size to obs and no_cells_exp to var. Loading into a directory that already holds an experiment overwrites its stores and drops any saved memory_py.*.

Several files. prescan_h5ad_files, prescan_tenx_h5_files and prescan_mtx_dirs read the gene sets first and fix the gene universe (intersection by default, or union), then load_multi_* loads against that prescan. obs gains exp_id and cell_id is prefixed with it. To combine experiments you already loaded, merge_sc_experiments keeps the shared genes and each input's kept cells, and carries no cache over.

Saving. obs and var edits go to the DuckDB at once. save writes what lives in memory: the cell filter, the HVG set and the cache, as memory_py.npz and memory_py.json. It does not write a fitted residual model, and warns. load_existing brings it all back, and restores the stores from counts.bxa if only the archive is left (archive_sc_exp). save_h5ad exports kept cells, obs, var and the embeddings and graph that still match to an h5ad file; write_h5ad_sc, write_tenx_h5_sc and write_cellranger_output write in-memory counts as files other tools read.

Test data. generate_single_cell_test_data plants cell types in synthetic counts. The generate_* twins serve the ADT, CellSweep and DIALOGUE examples. The download_* functions fetch the vignette data sets into ~/.cache/bixverse and return the path, or the cached one.

params = bv.params.SyntheticDataParams(n_cells=2000, n_genes=500)
sim = bv.io.generate_single_cell_test_data(params, seed=1)
sc = bv.io.load_csr("experiments/demo", sim.counts, sim.obs, sim.var)

bv.pp.find_hvg(sc, hvg_no=200)
bv.io.save(sc)
sc = bv.io.load_existing("experiments/demo")

Gotchas. The loaders want integral raw counts. load_h5ad finds them with detect_raw_count_slot, which prefers layers.counts, then raw.X, then X; set raw_count_slot if it picks wrong, and use load_h5ad_norm for files that only hold log-normalised values. load_mtx takes genes as rows, the 10x convention, unless cells_as_rows says otherwise; get_cell_ranger_params finds the three files for you. Nothing here needs h5py. A store in the old v3 format still opens with a warning, and upgrade_sc_store converts it.

Worked through in Single-cell data I/O in bixverse and Scaling to millions of cells with bixverse.

docs.title: Loading several files
docs.text:
Getting counts into an experiment directory, and back out.

Every loader takes the directory to create and returns the opened SingleCells. Pick the one for your format: load_csr for counts already in memory, load_h5ad, load_tenx_h5 or load_mtx for files, and the load_multi_* twins for several files in one go. After the first load you only need load_existing.

What a load does. It applies the cell and gene QC of MinQualityParams (by default at least 100 genes, 250 counts per cell and 10 cells per gene), so dropped cells and genes never enter the store. It then writes the cell-major and gene-major stores and loads obs and var into the DuckDB, adding nnz and lib_size to obs and no_cells_exp to var. Loading into a directory that already holds an experiment overwrites its stores and drops any saved memory_py.*.

Several files. prescan_h5ad_files, prescan_tenx_h5_files and prescan_mtx_dirs read the gene sets first and fix the gene universe (intersection by default, or union), then load_multi_* loads against that prescan. obs gains exp_id and cell_id is prefixed with it. To combine experiments you already loaded, merge_sc_experiments keeps the shared genes and each input's kept cells, and carries no cache over.

Saving. obs and var edits go to the DuckDB at once. save writes what lives in memory: the cell filter, the HVG set and the cache, as memory_py.npz and memory_py.json. It does not write a fitted residual model, and warns. load_existing brings it all back, and restores the stores from counts.bxa if only the archive is left (archive_sc_exp). save_h5ad exports kept cells, obs, var and the embeddings and graph that still match to an h5ad file; write_h5ad_sc, write_tenx_h5_sc and write_cellranger_output write in-memory counts as files other tools read.

Test data. generate_single_cell_test_data plants cell types in synthetic counts. The generate_* twins serve the ADT, CellSweep and DIALOGUE examples. The download_* functions fetch the vignette data sets into ~/.cache/bixverse and return the path, or the cached one.

params = bv.params.SyntheticDataParams(n_cells=2000, n_genes=500)
sim = bv.io.generate_single_cell_test_data(params, seed=1)
sc = bv.io.load_csr("experiments/demo", sim.counts, sim.obs, sim.var)

bv.pp.find_hvg(sc, hvg_no=200)
bv.io.save(sc)
sc = bv.io.load_existing("experiments/demo")

The loaders want integral raw counts. load_h5ad finds them with detect_raw_count_slot, which prefers layers.counts, then raw.X, then X; set raw_count_slot if it picks wrong, and use load_h5ad_norm for files that only hold log-normalised values. load_mtx takes genes as rows, the 10x convention, unless cells_as_rows says otherwise; get_cell_ranger_params finds the three files for you. Pick the one for your format: load_csr for counts already in memory, load_h5ad, load_tenx_h5 or load_mtx for files, and the load_multi_* twins for several files in one go. After the first load you only need load_existing.

What a load does. It applies the cell and gene QC of MinQualityParams (by default at least 100 genes, 250 counts per cell and 10 cells per gene), so dropped cells and genes never enter the store. It then writes the cell-major and gene-major stores and loads obs and var into the DuckDB, adding nnz and lib_size to obs and no_cells_exp to var. Loading into a directory that already holds an experiment overwrites its stores and drops any saved memory_py.*.

Several files. prescan_h5ad_files, prescan_tenx_h5_files and prescan_mtx_dirs read the gene sets first and fix the gene universe (intersection by default, or union), then load_multi_* loads against that prescan. obs gains exp_id and cell_id is prefixed with it. To combine experiments you already loaded, merge_sc_experiments keeps the shared genes and each input's kept cells, and carries no cache over.

Saving. obs and var edits go to the DuckDB at once. save writes what lives in memory: the cell filter, the HVG set and the cache, as memory_py.npz and memory_py.json. It does not write a fitted residual model, and warns. load_existing brings it all back, and restores the stores from counts.bxa if only the archive is left (archive_sc_exp). save_h5ad exports kept cells, obs, var and the embeddings and graph that still match to an h5ad file; write_h5ad_sc, write_tenx_h5_sc and write_cellranger_output write in-memory counts as files other tools read.

Test data. generate_single_cell_test_data plants cell types in synthetic counts. The generate_* twins serve the ADT, CellSweep and DIALOGUE examples. The download_* functions fetch the vignette data sets into ~/.cache/bixverse and return the path, or the cached one.

params = bv.params.SyntheticDataParams(n_cells=2000, n_genes=500)
sim = bv.io.generate_single_cell_test_data(params, seed=1)
sc = bv.io.load_csr("experiments/demo", sim.counts, sim.obs, sim.var)

bv.pp.find_hvg(sc, hvg_no=200)
bv.io.save(sc)
sc = bv.io.load_existing("experiments/demo")

Gotchas. The loaders want integral raw counts. load_h5ad finds them with detect_raw_count_slot, which prefers layers.counts, then raw.X, then X; set raw_count_slot if it picks wrong, and use load_h5ad_norm for files that only hold log-normalised values. load_mtx takes genes as rows, the 10x convention, unless cells_as_rows says otherwise; get_cell_ranger_params finds the three files for you. Nothing here needs h5py. A store in the old v3 format still opens with a warning, and upgrade_sc_store converts it.

docs.title: CellLoader
docs.text:
CellLoader(
    reader: CellReader,
    indices: Any = None,
    *,
    batch_size: int = 256,
    shuffle: bool = True,
    seed: int | None = None,
    layer: Layer = "norm",
    sparse: bool = True,
    prefetch: int = 4,
    drop_last: bool = False,
    genes: Any = None,
)

Iterate a cell-major store in minibatches, decoding ahead of the consumer.

Each pass spawns one feeder thread that decompresses and materialises batches into a bounded queue, so decode overlaps the training step. The queue depth is the backpressure knob, not a parallelism knob: decode is already rayon-parallel inside a single batch.

>>> import bixverse as bv
>>> reader = bv.CellReader("counts.bin")
>>> loader = bv.CellLoader(reader, batch_size=256)
>>> for batch in loader:
...     x = batch.scipy_csr()

Sparse is the default. A dense batch costs a zero-fill and a scatter over batch_size * n_genes floats no matter how few non-zeros it holds, which at droplet sparsity is roughly twenty times the memory traffic.

Build a loader.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default reader CellReader

An open cell-major CellReader.

required indices Any

Cells to iterate. None uses every cell in the store.

None batch_size int

Cells per batch.

256 shuffle bool

Reshuffle at the start of every epoch.

True seed int | None

Base seed for the shuffle. None draws one at random.

None layer Layer

"raw", "norm" or "both".

'norm' sparse bool

CSR components when true, a dense buffer when false.

True prefetch int

Batches held in flight by the feeder thread.

4 drop_last bool

Drop a trailing partial batch.

False genes Any

Store gene indices to keep, in the column order wanted. None keeps every gene.

None

Type Description ValueError

For a gene-major store, an unusable parameter, an out-of-range cell or gene index, or a repeated gene.

docs.title: Ligand-receptor
docs.text:
Ligand-receptor analysis, two ways: CellPhoneDB on the expression in your experiment, and NicheNet-style ligand activity and interaction prioritisation.

CellPhoneDB. get_cellphonedb_db fetches the v5 database (once, it is cached) and cellphonedb scores every interaction for every ordered pair of clusters in an obs column. method picks permutation p-values, a DEG-gated test or the plain means. The database speaks gene symbols: if your var ids are Ensembl, point gene_id_col at the symbol column.

NicheNet. Build a ligand to target influence matrix from a signalling and a gene regulatory network with generate_ligand_target_influence, or wrap one you already have with as_ligand_target_influence. ligand_activity_scores ranks the ligands against a gene set (the receiver's DEGs, say) within a background, compute_expression_info gives per-cluster expression of the ligands and receptors, and prioritise_interactions combines it all with the DE tables into one ranked table of sender, ligand, receiver, receptor.

What lands where. Nothing here writes to the experiment. Every function returns a polars frame or a LigandTargetInfluence. Only cellphonedb and compute_expression_info read the counts, and they take a SingleCells (kept cells only); the NicheNet steps work on the networks and tables you hand them. The DE tables come from you: bv.de.find_all_markers renamed to cluster_id, gene, lfc, pval does the job.

import numpy as np
import polars as pl

genes = sc.gene_ids().tolist()
ligands, receptors, tfs, targets = genes[:5], genes[5:10], genes[10:15], genes[20:120]
ppi = pl.DataFrame({"from": ligands + receptors, "to": receptors + tfs, "weight": 1.0})
grn = pl.DataFrame(
    {"from": [t for t in tfs for _ in range(20)], "to": targets, "weight": 1.0}
)

influence = bv.lr.generate_ligand_target_influence(ligands, ppi, grn)
activity = bv.lr.ligand_activity_scores(
    influence, {"degs": targets[:20]}, background=genes[:300]
).filter(pl.col("gene_set") == "degs")

# Per cluster DE and expression: yours would come from bv.de and the experiment
cell_types = sorted(sc.obs()["cell_grp"].unique().to_list())
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
n = len(cell_types) * len(genes)
celltype_de = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "cluster_id": np.repeat(cell_types, len(genes)),
        "gene": genes * len(cell_types),
        "lfc": rng.normal(size=n),
        "pval": rng.uniform(1e-6, 1, size=n),
    }
)
expr = bv.lr.compute_expression_info(sc, "cell_grp", ligands + receptors)
prio = bv.lr.prioritise_interactions(
    celltype_de,
    expr,
    activity,
    pl.DataFrame({"ligand": ligands, "receptor": receptors}),
    senders_oi=cell_types[:1],
    receivers_oi=cell_types[1:],
    scenario="one_condition",
)

# CellPhoneDB on the experiment, with an L/R table of your own
lr_db = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "interaction_id": [f"CPI{i}" for i in range(5)],
        "partner_a": ligands,
        "partner_b": receptors,
        "genes_a": [[g] for g in ligands],
        "genes_b": [[g] for g in receptors],
    }
)
cpdb = bv.lr.cellphonedb(
    sc, "cell_grp", lr_db, params=bv.params.CellphonedbParams(n_perm=100)
)

Gotchas. prioritise_interactions defaults to scenario="case_control", which weighs the condition terms and then refuses to run without a condition_de; pass scenario="one_condition" or your own weights when there is no contrast. It wants one row per ligand in ligand_activities: filter ligand_activity_scores down to a single gene set first. Ligand and receptor ids must be in the same namespace in the networks, the DE table and compute_expression_info, which reads var ids. cellphonedb drops interactions with a subunit missing from the experiment, with a warning, and errors if none are left. get_cellphonedb_db needs a download on first use.

Worked through in Ligand-receptor analysis with bixverse.

docs.title: cellphonedb
docs.text:
cellphonedb(
    sc: SingleCells,
    celltype_colname: str,
    lr_db: DataFrame,
    *,
    method: CpdbMethod = "statistical",
    deg_table: DataFrame | None = None,
    senders: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    receivers: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    gene_id_col: str = "gene_id",
    params: CellphonedbParams | None = None,
    verbose: Verbose = True,
) -> DataFrame

CellPhoneDB ligand-receptor analysis.

For every interaction and ordered (sender, receiver) cluster pair, partner a is measured in the sender and partner b in the receiver. The interaction mean is the average of the two partner means, zero if either is not expressed; a complex takes the minimum over its subunits. The gate needs both partners expressed in more than threshold of their cluster's cells.

  • "statistical": permutes the cluster labels, p = #(perm > real) / n_perm, 1 where the mean is zero or the gate fails.
  • "degs": no permutations; the gate also needs partner a to be a DEG of the sender or partner b of the receiver, as deg_table says.
  • "simple": the means and the expression gate only.

Reads the normalised layer of the L/R genes once. Interactions with a subunit missing from sc drop with a warning.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default sc SingleCells

The experiment.

required celltype_colname str

The cluster column in obs. Cells with a missing label are ignored.

required lr_db DataFrame

The database, see get_cellphonedb_db.

required method CpdbMethod

See above.

'statistical' deg_table DataFrame | None

cluster_id and gene, the DEGs per cluster. Needed for "degs", ignored with a warning otherwise.

None senders Sequence[str] | None

Restrict the pairs to these sender clusters. None uses all.

None receivers Sequence[str] | None

The same for the receivers.

None gene_id_col str

The var column holding the symbols used in lr_db. A duplicated symbol resolves to its first gene.

'gene_id' params CellphonedbParams | None

The parameters. None uses the defaults.

None verbose Verbose

0 (False) silent, 1 (True) progress, 2 extra detail where the method has it.

True

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

One row per interaction and pair: interaction_id, partner_a,

DataFrame

partner_b, sender, receiver, mean, pval (null unless

DataFrame

"statistical") and gate.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

On a malformed database, no testable interaction, an unknown sender or receiver, or "degs" without deg_table.

Examples:

>>> cpdb = bv.lr.cellphonedb(sc, "cell_grp", lr_db, method="simple")
>>> cpdb = bv.lr.cellphonedb(
...     sc,
...     "cell_grp",
...     lr_db,
...     senders=["cell_type_1"],
...     params=bv.params.CellphonedbParams(n_perm=200, threshold=0.05),
... )
References

Efremova, et al., Nat. Protoc., 2020; Troulé, et al., Nat. Protoc., 2025.

Build a ligand to target influence matrix from a signalling and a gene regulatory network with generate_ligand_target_influence, or wrap one you already have with as_ligand_target_influence. ligand_activity_scores ranks the ligands against a gene set (the receiver's DEGs, say) within a background, compute_expression_info gives per-cluster expression of the ligands and receptors, and prioritise_interactions combines it all with the DE tables into one ranked table of sender, ligand, receiver, receptor.

What lands where. Nothing here writes to the experiment. Every function returns a polars frame or a LigandTargetInfluence. Only cellphonedb and compute_expression_info read the counts, and they take a SingleCells (kept cells only); the NicheNet steps work on the networks and tables you hand them. The DE tables come from you: bv.de.find_all_markers renamed to cluster_id, gene, lfc, pval does the job.

import numpy as np
import polars as pl

genes = sc.gene_ids().tolist()
ligands, receptors, tfs, targets = genes[:5], genes[5:10], genes[10:15], genes[20:120]
ppi = pl.DataFrame({"from": ligands + receptors, "to": receptors + tfs, "weight": 1.0})
grn = pl.DataFrame(
    {"from": [t for t in tfs for _ in range(20)], "to": targets, "weight": 1.0}
)

influence = bv.lr.generate_ligand_target_influence(ligands, ppi, grn)
activity = bv.lr.ligand_activity_scores(
    influence, {"degs": targets[:20]}, background=genes[:300]
).filter(pl.col("gene_set") == "degs")

# Per cluster DE and expression: yours would come from bv.de and the experiment
cell_types = sorted(sc.obs()["cell_grp"].unique().to_list())
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
n = len(cell_types) * len(genes)
celltype_de = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "cluster_id": np.repeat(cell_types, len(genes)),
        "gene": genes * len(cell_types),
        "lfc": rng.normal(size=n),
        "pval": rng.uniform(1e-6, 1, size=n),
    }
)
expr = bv.lr.compute_expression_info(sc, "cell_grp", ligands + receptors)
prio = bv.lr.prioritise_interactions(
    celltype_de,
    expr,
    activity,
    pl.DataFrame({"ligand": ligands, "receptor": receptors}),
    senders_oi=cell_types[:1],
    receivers_oi=cell_types[1:],
    scenario="one_condition",
)

# CellPhoneDB on the experiment, with an L/R table of your own
lr_db = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "interaction_id": [f"CPI{i}" for i in range(5)],
        "partner_a": ligands,
        "partner_b": receptors,
        "genes_a": [[g] for g in ligands],
        "genes_b": [[g] for g in receptors],
    }
)

    sc, "cell_grp", lr_db, params=bv.params.CellphonedbParams(n_perm=100)

docs.title: Meta cells
docs.text:
Meta cell generators, quality metrics, merging and persistence.

Four generators collapse a store into far fewer meta cells held in memory as a MetaCells: bootstrapped neighbourhoods (hdWGCNA), SEACells, SuperCells and MetaCells2. Start with one of them, then judge the result with the metrics, and run the usual bv.pp, bv.graph and bv.embed calls on the MetaCells itself. save_metacells and load_metacells write and read a meta cell set as a directory.

What lands where. The generators take a SingleCells or SingleCellsSubset, leave it alone and return a new MetaCells. calc_meta_cell_purity writes mc_purity (and optional label and entropy columns) to the meta cells' obs, calc_diffusion_coordinates writes density_region to obs and dcs, density_dist and regions to mc.other_data, and calc_manifold_metrics writes compactness and separation to obs. get_meta_cell_purity, calc_meta_cell_compactness and calc_meta_cell_separation return a frame and touch nothing. Each meta cell keeps the store cells it aggregates in obs original_cell_idx. merge_meta_cells and meta_cells_per_group return a new object.

Object types. The generators accept SingleCells and SingleCellsSubset; the metrics and merge_meta_cells take MetaCells.

mc = bv.metacells.generate_supercells(
    sc, params=bv.params.SupercellParams(graining_factor=20)
)
bv.metacells.calc_meta_cell_purity(mc, sc.obs()["cell_grp"].to_list())
bv.metacells.calc_diffusion_coordinates(mc, sc.cache.knn)
bv.metacells.calc_manifold_metrics(mc)
mc.obs(cols=["meta_cell_id", "mc_purity", "compactness", "separation"])

From there the meta cells go through the normal chain:

bv.pp.find_hvg(mc, hvg_no=500)
bv.pp.calculate_pca(mc, no_pcs=10)
bv.graph.find_neighbours(mc)

Gotchas. Bootstrapped, SEACells and SuperCells read the cached PCA and kNN of the source (or build the kNN again with regenerate_knn=True), so run bv.pp.find_hvg, bv.pp.calculate_pca and bv.graph.find_neighbours on sc first. A stale PCA or kNN raises. Without a kNN, the bootstrapped and SuperCells generators warn and return None, SEACells raises. MetaCells2 works on the raw counts and needs neither. Bootstrapped meta cells overlap; the others partition, and MetaCells2 leaves outlier cells unassigned. The labels for the purity are one per row of the source obs, or one per kept cell. The diffusion map is built from the source kNN, so pass sc.cache.knn, and calc_manifold_metrics needs calc_diffusion_coordinates first. A merged object has several index spaces, so both of them warn and do nothing on it: run them per source before merge_meta_cells. Merging also drops the caches and the HVGs, so redo the chain afterwards. The residual model is not saved.

Worked through in Meta cells with bixverse.

    sc, params=bv.params.SupercellParams(graining_factor=20)

bv.metacells.calc_diffusion_coordinates(mc, sc.cache.knn)

docs.title: calc_meta_cell_purity
docs.text:
calc_meta_cell_purity(
    mc: MetaCells,
    original_cell_type: Sequence[str | None],
    *,
    add_additional_info: PurityInfo = "none",
    add_entropy: bool = False,
) -> None

Label purity of each meta cell, written to obs.

Adds mc_purity (fraction of the meta cell's cells carrying its most common label), and on request mc_top_label, mc_second_label (null for a pure meta cell), mc_second_frac and mc_entropy (Shannon entropy of the labels over log(number of distinct labels), 0 with a single label). Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mc MetaCells

The meta cells.

required original_cell_type Sequence[str | None]

Labels of the source cells, either one per obs row of the source (sc.obs()) or one per kept cell in cells_to_keep order; the length decides which. Cells in no meta cell may be missing (None).

required add_additional_info PurityInfo

"none", "top_label" or "top_two_labels".

'none' add_entropy bool

Add mc_entropy.

False

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the labels fit neither cell space.

Examples:

>>> labels = sc.obs()["cell_grp"].to_list()
>>> bv.metacells.calc_meta_cell_purity(mc, labels, add_entropy=True)
>>> mc.obs(cols=["meta_cell_id", "mc_purity", "mc_entropy"])

docs.title: calc_diffusion_coordinates
docs.text:
calc_diffusion_coordinates(
    mc: MetaCells,
    knn: KnnGraph,
    *,
    n_dcs: int = 10,
    k_density: int = 150,
    seed: int = 42,
    verbose: Verbose = True,
) -> None

Diffusion map of the source cells and a density region per meta cell.

Builds multiscale diffusion components off the source kNN, takes the distance to the k_density-th neighbour in that space as a density proxy and tags its lower quartile "high", upper quartile "low", the rest "mid". Each meta cell gets the most common region of its cells in obs density_region (ties to the name that sorts first); other_data gains dcs, density_dist and regions.

A merged object warns and is left alone: its memberships live in several index spaces.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mc MetaCells

The meta cells.

required knn KnnGraph

The kNN of the source cells, one row per kept cell in the source's cells_to_keep order, e.g. sc.cache.knn.

required n_dcs int

Diffusion components.

10 k_density int

The neighbour giving the density.

150 seed int

Seed.

42 verbose Verbose

0 (False) silent, 1 (True) progress, 2 extra detail where the method has it.

True

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the kNN does not cover the kept source cells.

References

Persad, et al., Nat Biotechnol, 2023.

Examples:

>>> bv.metacells.calc_diffusion_coordinates(mc, sc.cache.knn, n_dcs=10)
>>> dcs = mc.other_data["dcs"]

docs.title: calc_manifold_metrics
docs.text:
calc_manifold_metrics(mc: MetaCells) -> None

Compactness and separation of each meta cell in the diffusion map.

Compactness is the mean variance over the diffusion components of a meta cell's cells, lower is better; separation the distance from its centroid to the nearest other centroid, higher is better. Both go to obs. Needs calc_diffusion_coordinates first; without it, or on a merged object, a warning and nothing changes.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mc MetaCells

The meta cells.

required References

Persad, et al., Nat Biotechnol, 2023.

Examples:

>>> bv.metacells.calc_diffusion_coordinates(mc, sc.cache.knn)
>>> bv.metacells.calc_manifold_metrics(mc)
